items.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021
items.q: The interviewer states 'you were associated a little bit with James Moody', but the interviewee does not confirm this association or describe any personal interaction, instead discussing his own musical studies.

ctx.x: No, music was what I wanted, it was the only thing that keep me well being, the music was doing me good and I did everything for the music.

You could have decided at the time, after World War II bop was starting to become, you know, the way to play I guess. And you were associated a little bit with James Moody. Were you looking for something else besides bebop?
No, I was playing music, so I went to the conservatory and studied under Delacluse, the clarinetist and it was getting my technique up and classical music and everything. All music.
